questions.question_text: Vectors $\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b}$ have $|\underset{\sim}{a}| = 10$, $|\underset{\sim}{b}| = 4$ and $\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b} = -28$. Find the angle between them, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Dropped the negative sign and gave the acute supplement instead of the obtuse angle.
Gave the reflex angle; the angle between two vectors is always taken in $[0^{\circ},180^{\circ}]$.
Divided by $|\underset{\sim}{a}|^2|\underset{\sim}{b}|^2 = 1600$ instead of $|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}| = 40$.

questions.question_text: Find the angle between $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Ignored the negative cosine and gave the acute supplement instead of the obtuse angle.
Subtracted the component products, $(7)(-3)-(1)(5) = -26$, instead of adding them.
Divided by $|\underset{\sim}{a}|^2|\underset{\sim}{b}|^2 = 1700$ instead of $|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|$.

questions.question_text: Find the angle between $\underset{\sim}{u} = 8\underset{\sim}{i}+6\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v} = 2\underset{\sim}{i}+7\underset{\sim}{j}$, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Took $\sin^{-1}$ of $0.7967$ instead of $\cos^{-1}$.
Subtracted the correct angle from $180^{\circ}$; the cosine is positive, so the angle is acute.
Added the components to get the magnitudes ($8+6$ and $2+7$) instead of using $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$.

questions.question_text: Find the angle between $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Ignored the negative cosine and gave the acute supplement instead of the obtuse angle.
Added the magnitudes ($3+5 = 8$) instead of multiplying them in the denominator.
Assumed the zero $y$-component of $\underset{\sim}{b}$ makes the vectors perpendicular; the dot product is $-2$, not $0$.

questions.question_text: Find the exact value of $\cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Lost the negative sign of the dot product $(1)(3)+(5)(-1) = -2$.
Subtracted the component products, $(1)(3)-(5)(-1) = 8$, instead of adding them.
Simplified $\sqrt{26}\times\sqrt{10} = \sqrt{260}$ as $\sqrt{65}$ instead of $2\sqrt{65}$.

questions.question_text: The points $A(2,-1)$, $B(6,2)$ and $C(-3,-4)$ are given. Find $\angle BAC$, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Used $\overrightarrow{BA}$ in place of $\overrightarrow{AB}$, which reverses the sign and gives the supplement.
Gave the reflex angle; the angle between two vectors is always taken in $[0^{\circ},180^{\circ}]$.
Used $|\overrightarrow{AC}|^2 = 34$ instead of $|\overrightarrow{AC}| = \sqrt{34}$ in the denominator.

questions.question_text: The angle between $\begin{pmatrix} p \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ is $60^{\circ}$, where $p > 0$. Find $p$.

options.why: Solved $p^2 = 3$ but forgot to take the square root.
Used $\cos 60^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, confusing it with $\cos 30^{\circ}$.
Used $\cos 45^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ in place of $\cos 60^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.question_text: Vectors $\underset{\sim}{u}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v}$ have $|\underset{\sim}{u}| = 3\sqrt{2}$, $|\underset{\sim}{v}| = 4$ and $\underset{\sim}{u}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v} = -12$. Find the exact angle between them.

options.why: Dropped the negative sign and gave the acute supplement instead of the obtuse angle.
Gave the reflex angle; the angle between two vectors is always taken in $[0^{\circ},180^{\circ}]$.
Read $-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ as $-\dfrac{1}{2}$ when taking the inverse cosine.
